Audit1682 original abrupt-reboot regression — executable historical lab route

This is a supplemental physical procedure, not a recorded pass. It addresses the
specific Thor gap left by the current-updater rehearsal: an old updater fsyncs the
capsule FILE but not its vfat directory. The real immediate kernel reboot is the
fault injection. No power switch, cache/sysctl tuning, forced storage failure or
invented trigger API is needed. Real arbitrary power-cut timing is not claimed.

The evidence chain is source-specific:
  Agent fix: 7c2d5787b7e1cfc7347caa700e6e1bfe584125f2
  Old updater: 2ef50a953e29809f2bd2a59df0f50625e2030289
  Updater durability fix, excluded here: cb2c7b5a5ed67c7f3d9d04315e32bdd3902024e9
  Incident/design: 2af488bb16295e78200432caa3a59bee92572558
The pinned old updater permits capsule staging only on tegra264 (AGX Thor);
its Orin branch performs a rootfs-only switch. This historical route therefore
REFUSES Orin. Qualifying another historical Orin updater is a separate task, not
a reason to override its allowlist.

The latter records the same-image Thor failure: no ESRT attempt, unchanged
firmware/slot, then verifier rollback. A new updater's Syncfs can make the old
Agent control pass; that is not a sensitive test of the Agent fix.

Prepare off-device

1. Reserve only physical serial @SERIAL@ with the capsule plan's exact ECID,
   board, disk serial, APP/APP_b/ESP UUIDs and vendor-qualified forward capsule.
   Independently authorize all destructive preparation, each update/reboot and
   recovery. Use the existing capsule plan's stable power, complete console and
   anti-rollback/recovery requirements. No production workload or credentials.
   Normal legacy Agent operations use the authenticated direct CLI endpoint;
   local console is reserved for identity observations and authorized recovery.

2. Make clean private source worktrees at the two exact commits above. Do not
   reset a user checkout. The initial image must actually be @OS@ and run the
   affected updater SHA256 @UPDATER@ from the pinned producer record; do not edit
   os-release to force the workaround. Its copyFileSync has file.Sync but no
   Syncfs, parent fsync, rename-plus-dirsync or post-install wrapper sync. Review
   the shipped initial image and installed binary; record go version -m output,
   producer/toolchain/build command, source commit and SHA256. A provenance gap,
   different updater or sync performed by a wrapper disqualifies sensitivity.
   Do not install a historical updater into an unrelated production OS.

3. Generator inventory fields: capsule_plan (the existing1682 evidence.json),
   agent_source, updater_source, nonce (independent32hex), running_os,
   legacy_updater_binary and legacy_producer_record. The producer JSON must bind
   source_revision, binary_sha256, running_os and reviewer. Run on the host:
     python3 .github/regression-coverage/manual/jetson-capsule-boundary.py inventory.json NEW_OUTPUT
   Generation hashes inputs and emits source overlays, image files, build commands
   and all-not_run evidence. It neither builds nor installs anything automatically.

4. In @SOURCE@ execute the exact generated build command for each required
   variant. All are Linux/arm64, CGO disabled, -mod=readonly and -trimpath, with
   Go toolchain1.26.5 and output only in @OUTPUT@. Record Go version, complete command/exit, overlay
   hashes and output SHA256. All five binary hashes must be distinct; identical
   outputs mean an overlay was not applied and disqualify the build. The generator
   canonicalizes source paths (including /tmp symlinks) for Go overlay matching.
   Never distribute these lab binaries as a release.
   Source variants differ ONLY as recorded:
   fixed: unchanged production code from the original fix.
   historical-instant: post-install call is the actual immediate reboot syscall,
     with no sync/clean request; matches the pre-fix boundary. The now-unused OS
     version read is removed. It adds no tracing, reads, pauses or flushing.
   sync-only: post-install calls the actual production reboot(), preserving
     unix.Sync followed by the immediate syscall, with no clean shutdown.
   clean-request-failure: only the systemctl function dependency returns an
     explicit injected error; production sync and immediate fallback still run.
   watchdog-no-reboot: only that dependency returns nil WITHOUT requesting a
     reboot; production sync, full unchanged60-second sleep and real immediate
     fallback still run. This simulates an acknowledged request that did not
     reboot, not an actual hung PID1/storage driver. No shortened timer.

5. Independently review and include EVERY file in generated image-files in BOTH
   the prepared initial root and the candidate image. Include Python3 and the
   existing util-linux/nvbootctrl tools. The candidate must carry the unchanged
   fixed Agent, the intended updater and the same exact capsule/marker; it must
   not boot one of the dangerous lab variants after success. Recompute archive,
   descriptor and capsule-plan hashes for these instrumented images. The existing
   payload inspection must additionally record path/mode/SHA256 for every
   generated observer/config/unit/drop-in, the candidate fixed Agent and capsule.
   Do not reuse an artifact digest from before these image changes. This is a
   two-stage preparation: generate/build the instrumentation first; produce and
   inspect the instrumented initial/candidate images; regenerate the capsule
   plan with their final hashes; regenerate this boundary package in a NEW output
   directory with the SAME nonce/board. Require every embedded observer/config/
   unit/drop-in byte to match the final package. Build commands/output paths may
   change, so re-record the actual final binaries. The candidate URL in generated
   device-commands.json must refer to that final inspected image.

6. Check systemd unit ordering OFFLINE against both actual image unit sets:
     systemd-analyze verify PATH_TO_IMAGE_UNITS
   PATH_TO_IMAGE_UNITS means the independently extracted image's actual observer,
   Agent and updater unit files plus drop-ins with their real paths, not a host
   wildcard. Use systemd-analyze --root on a complete isolated image tree if its
   tool version supports it. Do not start or reload the host system manager.
   On the prepared target BEFORE staging, read the live merged units with:
     timeout 15 systemctl cat ci1682-observe.service
     timeout 15 systemctl cat wendyos-update-verify.service wendyos-update-commit.service wendy-agent.service
     timeout 15 systemctl show ci1682-observe.service --property=ActiveState,SubState,Result,Before
   Each verifier/commit/Agent unit must REQUIRE and start AFTER the observer.
   The observer has a60-second limit, its whole process group is systemd-owned,
   and failure prevents those units starting. A failure is a lab STOP, not a pass;
   recover only over the reserved console. Do not remove ordering to get green.

7. The actual observer runs after local-fs/data mounts, BEFORE verifier/Agent
   cleanup, on every boot. It verifies DT serial/SoC and ESP GPT/parent disk, then
   records boot ID, root major/minor, nvbootctrl slots/firmware, ESRT, OsIndications
   and exact capsule presence/hash. If ESP is not mounted it creates a unique
   /run directory and mounts only that verified block device read-only, then
   unmounts only its own mount. Existing mounts are never remounted/unmounted.
   It writes an exclusive boot record to /data/ci1682/@NONCE@/BOOT_ID.json and
   CI1682_BOOT_OBSERVATION to the serial console/journal. Readonly evidence is
   taken AFTER firmware, so it cannot flush the pre-reboot vulnerable directory.
   A post-Agent manual inspection is insufficient: rollback may delete capsules.

8. Reboot the prepared baseline normally once, before starting the experiment.
   Require successful observer completion, full console record with this nonce,
   known boot ID, no pending deployment, exact old firmware/slot, no capsule and
   no active capsule-delivery request. Verify the installed old updater hash and
   current root image identity. Read these on the reserved console:
     cat /etc/os-release
     sha256sum /usr/bin/wendyos-update
     timeout 15 systemctl show wendy-agent.service --property=MainPID,ActiveState,SubState
   Hash /proc/ACTUAL_MAIN_PID/exe with sha256sum, then re-read MainPID to exclude
   a process replacement while observing. Match the recorded observer/config/unit hashes.
   Stop on any failed/ambiguous check. Do not touch ESP, sync, unmount it, run a
   storage diagnostic or attach a debugger BETWEEN staging and the test reboot.

Run the sensitive before/after pair

9. First run generated deploy_historical-instant (Agent upload only), and verify
   the live executable hash using step8. Every deploy_* command uses --json,
   which uploads and verifies the Agent and skips the OS-update step; never add
   --yes to it, because without --artifact-url that applies the latest public
   OS. Start uninterrupted external serial
   capture, then run generated update_historical-instant, which pins that same
   exact --binary and the final instrumented --artifact-url. This is the real Agent install path, not console
   install followed by a manual delayed reboot. Keep update_* in text mode (no --json).
   Confirm the CLI actually deployed this binary before it requests the update;
   preserve its version/upload evidence and the installed executable hash from
   the separate pre-update deployment observation if needed. If the CLI cannot
   establish the intended binary, stop; do not infer it from the filename.
   The candidate format/min_tool_version must be supported by the exact old
   updater; choose a qualified compatible artifact, never bypass its admission
   guard. Candidate image/capsule, initial OS/updater, board and source/binary identities
   must be recorded. Observe at most the capsule plan's install/boot bounds.

10. The old-control failure is valid ONLY with all of these actual observations:
    installer successfully staged the exact candidate and requested the reboot;
    a new boot ID; earliest observer record BEFORE verifier/Agent cleanup shows
    no staged capsule; ESRT last_attempt_version/status unchanged with no new
    capsule processing in the serial firmware transcript; old firmware and old
    root/boot chain remain; verifier reports running!=target and subsequent
    rollback corresponds to that same attempted artifact. An ESRT rejection,
    wrong capsule, unsupported firmware, failed install, missing observer record,
    cleanup-before-observation or transport error is not the required failure.
    A control that succeeds is INCONCLUSIVE, never a pass: writeback may already
    have completed. Preserve that run and do not artificially weaken durability.

11. After an accepted control failure, require the exact original baseline again:
    old firmware/slot, healthy Agent, no pending deployment, exact old updater,
    empty ESP capsule path and no armed capsule indication. Retain the failed
    trial's observer record externally before any qualified recovery. If rollback
    does not produce the baseline, use only the separately authorized recovery.
    Run generated deploy_fixed, verify its live executable hash, then update_fixed
   with the unchanged fixed Agent and IDENTICAL
    candidate/capsule. No manual console install or sync is inserted.

12. Require actual clean-handover log on the affected OS, a new boot, earliest
    observer evidence and serial firmware processing of the intended capsule,
    the expected new ESRT/firmware version and target root/boot chain, followed
    by successful verified commit. A consumed/deleted capsule is expected only
    together with those fresh firmware/slot observations; absence alone fails.
    Reboot normally a second time and require persistent new firmware/root/Agent
    identity. This before-failure/after-success pair is the smallest rigorous
    human route for the ORIGINAL1682 regression, with no external trigger rig.

Isolate sync and exercise the fallback (separately qualified baselines)

13. A firmware transition can advance anti-rollback state. Do not pretend a
    rootfs reflash restores firmware. Use a separately qualified complete recovery
    or a matched reserved board with its own regenerated identity/config for each
    positive trial. Keep exact same capsule transition and old updater. Run the
    sync-only variant through the identical Agent install path; require successful
    firmware application and target boot. The valid old-control failure plus this
    result establishes the actual sync-before-immediate-reboot durability, without
    relying on systemd unmounts. No mount/ESP observation is inserted before reboot.

14. For the clean-request-failure variant require the explicit injected-request
    log, actual immediate reboot and the same successful physical durability
    observations. For watchdog-no-reboot require the normal clean-path log then
    the unchanged60-second grace and fallback log followed by actual reboot.
    Use external console capture timestamps (host monotonic timestamps), with no
    reboot before60 seconds and at most90 seconds to reset under an idle reserved
    lab load. Require firmware/target boot and second-boot persistence as above.
    If the process dies early, a service restarts it, the reboot never occurs or
    evidence is missing, fail the fixture; do not count a manual reboot.
    These real-reboot variants validate the injected dependency-failure outcomes;
    they do not claim an actual physically hung systemd/unmount was reproduced.

15. Preserve every binary/overlay/source/image/capsule hash, command exit, initial
    and earliest postboot records, external serial trace, firmware/ESRT transition,
    actual observer-before-verifier ordering, rollback/commit and second boot.
    Record failed/inconclusive/not_run distinctly. Recover the reserved device
    with its approved normal image after the trials, verify the normal Agent,
    and retain public evidence before removing only this nonce's lab material.
    Never ship the historical/direct-reboot or fake-clean-request variants.

Limits: this procedure supplies the actual source instrumentation and boot
observer; hardware execution/build results remain pending until recorded. It
cannot force spontaneous writeback to stay dirty. If the exact old control does
not exhibit loss, sensitivity remains unproven on that board/firmware/storage.
There is no claim of arbitrary power-cut, firmware-write interruption, unknown
old releases, or new-updater behavior from this historical experiment.
